title: Digital gravity: build sustainable, high-volume content and email distribution
summary: Cody Schneider explains his "digital gravity" view of marketing: pick repeatable channels (X, email nurture, newsletters, podcasts, short-form clips), publish at high volume, read the data, and double down on winners. He covers recycling top tweets, growing newsletters from social, pairing podcasts with newsletters for trust, and setting a North Star metric per channel.

principles.text: Think of marketing as building digital mass: more content creates more gravity and a larger natural inbound over time.
principles.quote: you're trying to build like digital Mass on the internet so that you have more digital gravity within your sphere

principles.text: Choose marketing you can sustain indefinitely, as a lifestyle choice rather than a campaign; consistency beats short bursts.
principles.quote: think about it as okay this is a lifestyle choice that I'm going to choose and for the next whatever it is you know five years I'm going to do this every week every day

principles.text: Run content as a volume-plus-data loop: publish a lot, check what works, do more of it and less of what doesn't.
principles.quote: do a bunch of stuff look at the data to see what works do more of what's working un less of what isn't and you're going to create a growth flywheel

principles.text: Recycle your top-performing posts every six to eight weeks; audiences have short attention spans.
principles.quote: I don't write new tweets anymore I basically just go and look at the top performers and I cycle them in every six to two months or six weeks to two months

principles.text: Pair a weekly podcast with a newsletter: repeated long-form listening builds deep trust so prospects arrive sales-ready.
principles.quote: you just build this such deep trust that by the time they come to sales they're like oh I'm buy ready like I know your whole stick

principles.text: Define one North Star metric per channel up front and get everyone to agree on it.
principles.quote: defining that Northstar goal from the beginning and having everybody agree on that that's how uh you like build good marketing organizations
